title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Marketing - Testimonials
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal wishes to place a client testimonial on their website. The client writes: "This paralegal won my impossible case and got me $100,000!" In reality, the case settled for $20,000. Is this permissible if the client genuinely wrote the testimonial without prompting?
options: Yes, because the paralegal cannot control what a client writes.
No, marketing rules require all statements—even client testimonials—to be demonstrably true, accurate, and verifiable.
Yes, as long as the paralegal adds a disclaimer saying 'past results do not guarantee future performance.'
No, client testimonials are banned entirely for paralegals.
questions.explain: Rule 8.03. Marketing must not be false or misleading. A paralegal cannot publish or allow to be published a testimonial that contains a material misrepresentation of fact, even if the client wrote it. The paralegal must refuse to post the inaccurate testimonial.
